entities.summary:
Honda Motor Co., Ltd., founded by Soichiro Honda and Takeo Fujisawa in Tokyo in 1948, is Japan's second-largest automaker and the world's largest motorcycle manufacturer — producing 4 million cars and 19 million motorcycles annually, with the world's most fuel-efficient internal combustion engines (VTEC, i-VTEC) and the first commercially successful hydrogen fuel cell vehicle (FCX Clarity, 2008). Honda's founding story — Soichiro Honda, a mechanical genius without business skills, partnering with Fujisawa's business genius — is a textbook study in complementary co-founder partnership.

Honda's motorcycle breakthrough — the Super Cub (1958), the world's best-selling motor vehicle of all time at 100+ million units produced — transformed personal mobility across Asia and developing nations. The Super Cub's simplicity, reliability, and affordability democratized transportation in countries where automobiles were unaffordable: Honda's 1960s advertising ('You meet the nicest people on a Honda') changed the social perception of motorcycles from dangerous outlaw machines to mainstream transport.

Honda's Formula One dominance (1986-1991, 6 Constructors' Championships; 2000-2006, 7 Constructors' Championships through partnerships with Williams, McLaren, and BAR) made it the most successful engine supplier in F1 history. The CVCC engine (1972) — the first to meet California's strict emission standards without a catalytic converter — demonstrated Honda's emissions engineering leadership. Honda's ASIMO humanoid robot (2000) advanced bipedal robotics; the Honda Jet (2015) entered business aviation. Honda's diverse technology portfolio — cars, motorcycles, jets, robots, power equipment — is the broadest of any company its size.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Honda's Super Cub — the world's best-selling motor vehicle at 100+ million units — democratized personal mobility across Asia and the developing world, and Honda's engineering culture (from VTEC to hydrogen fuel cells to humanoid robots) demonstrates that automotive excellence is a platform for the broadest possible mechanical innovation.
